data.content_ref: inline:SRC_002 argues the panel wins via a meta-cognitive System 2 delay induced by the checklist. But the problem explicitly asks for evidence that distinguishes genuine reliability gain from mere checklist compliance that happens to track the right answer. The target's proposed mechanism—slower processing and evidence-gathering—does not distinguish the two: a panel that is merely complying with the checklist also experiences the same temporal delay and explicit evidence-gathering per item, yet may be tracking the right answer for the wrong reasons. The target addresses the relative performance of panel vs. expert but never provides the requested evidence to separate genuine reliability from coincidental compliance.
